  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

  The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
  agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the
  Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to
  (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker, not to exceed a total of (8)
  eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is heard. In order to be recognized and
  present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the
  beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers
  are taken in the order slips are submitted.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
  public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
  meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
  meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
  conditions imposed.

  Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
  item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative
  or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire
  Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on
 Malibu Arts Commission  -Page - 3 -  August 27, 2024

  the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted.
  Public speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no
  final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow
  the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

  Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in
  the Community Services Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are available
  for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and 7:30
  a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours of the Commission meeting
  are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff
  reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page. Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least
  72 hours prior to the meeting.

  The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf
  (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the
  Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda
  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting
  will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104
  ADD Title II].

  Requests to show an audio or video presentation during a Commission meeting should be directed to the Media Team at
  media@malibucity.org. Material must be submitted by 12:00 p.m. on the meeting day.

  I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted
  in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 22nd day of August 2024, at 2:30 p.m.

   MINUTES
  MALIBU ARTS COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 25, 2024
  CITY HALL, MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  9:30 A.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Lawrence called the meeting to order at 9:31 a.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Fireball Lawrence; Vice Chair Julia Holland; and Commissioners Lotte
  Cherin, Barry Haldeman, and Peter Jones

  ABSENT: Ex-Officio Graeme Clifford

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Clove Galilee,
  Recreation Manager; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Jones moved, and Commissioner Cherin seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the meeting agenda was properly posted on
  June 20, 2024.

ITEM 1.  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Introduction of Recreation Manager Clove Galilee

  Community Services Director Riesgo introduced Recreation Manager Galilee.
  She stated that Recreation Manager Galilee would oversee programs related to
  arts, special events, and the Senior Center.

  Recreation Manager Galilee introduced herself and discussed her experience
  working in recreation and arts programming.

  B.  Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  Chair Lawrence opened the nominations for Chair.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting
  Minutes of June 25, 2024
  Page 2 of 4
  ________________________________

  Commissioner Cherin nominated Chair Lawrence to keep his position as Chair.

  Commissioner Jones nominated Chair Lawrence and Vice Chair Holland to keep
  their positions as Chair and Vice Chair.

  Commissioner Haldeman indicated agreement with Commissioners Cherin and
  Jones.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission voted to keep Chair Lawrence and Vice Chair
  Holland in their respective positions as Chair and Vice Chair.

ITEM 2.A.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  John Johannessen stated he supported and was interested in the Arts Commission
  projects. He stated City Council approved three Malibu Film Society events at
  Malibu City Hall.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION AD HOC COMMITTEE REPORTS

  1.  Arts in Education

  Community Services Director Riesgo student poetry workshop would occur
  during the 2024-25 school year, and scheduling would begin in August.

  2.  Malibu Public Art Exhibitions

  Chair Lawrence stated that forty-two artists were selected for the
  Community Surf Exhibition. He stated that Pep Williams was promoting
  his exhibition, and his artwork was featured in the ACCA Journal Magazine.

  3.  Business and Community Outreach

  In response to Commissioner Haldeman, Commissioner Jones stated City
  Council would review the Temporary Use Permit Ordinance in August.

  4.  Social Media

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented a video on the Pep
  Williams art exhibition.

  Chair Lawrence requested staff to tag him on social media when art-related
  items are posted so he could share them on his social media platforms.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Holland moved, and Chair Lawrence seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1. Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 28, 2024 Malibu Arts
  Commission Regular Meeting.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu City Gallery Art Exhibition Schedule
  Recommended Action: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
  Hoc Committee recommendation regarding the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Malibu City
  Gallery art exhibitions.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Lawrence stated the Commission would partner with the Frederick R.
  Weisman Museum of Art at Pepperdine University to feature five artists for the
  holiday themed still-life exhibition.

  Vice Chair Holland stated artist Sue Wong was excited to show her fashion designs
  at the Malibu City Gallery.

  Commissioner Cherin stated she preferred to showcase new artists rather than
  artists that have already exhibited at the Malibu City Gallery such as Kathy and
  Dan Eldon.

  Chair Lawrence stated he was unaware that Kathy Eldon had a previous art
  exhibition at the Malibu City Gallery.

  In response to Chair Lawrence, Commissioner Cherin stated she wanted to review
  options for new artists and did not support Kathy and Dan Eldon’s Art of Journaling
  exhibition for Fiscal Year 2024-25.
   Malibu Arts Commission Regular Meeting

  Vice Chair Holland stated she was working with several new artists, but most were
  not available during Fiscal Year 2024-25.

MOTION  Chair Lawrence moved, and Commissioner Jones seconded a motion to approve
  the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Malibu City Gallery art exhibition schedule with a Derek
  Schimming Retrospective and the Malibu Arts Association, a Still Life Holiday
  Show, Student Art Exhibition, and Sue Wong Fashion Design Exhibition;
  excluding the Art of Journaling exhibition by Kathy and Dan Eldon. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on summer CineMalibu
  movies in the park series and the Malibu Film Society.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Chair Lawrence stated the Art Talks series has concluded and artist interviews
  would take place at opening and closing art receptions.

  Vice Chair Holland stated she was working with a new band to provide live
  entertainment at the opening reception of A Tale of a Seaside Town.

  Commissioner Jones suggested adding new signs on the second floor of City Hall
  that would direct guests to the Malibu City Gallery.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Marketing

ADJOURNMENT

  At 11:05 a.m., Chair Lawrence adjourned the meeting.

  Approved and adopted by the Malibu Arts

  2024.

Subject:  Malibu City Gallery Exhibition Schedule

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and approve the Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad
Hoc Committee’s recommendation to feature Indigenous artists in connection with the 25th
Annual Chumash Day Powwow and Intertribal Gathering.

DISCUSSION: At the June 25, 2024 Regular meeting, the Commission reviewed and
approved five Malibu City Gallery Art Exhibitions for Fiscal Year 2024-25 including,

  •  Derek Shimming Retrospective and the Malibu Arts Association
  •  Still Life Holiday Show
  •  Student Art Exhibition
  •  Sue Wong Fashion Design Exhibition
  •  Malibu Surf Culture Community Art Exhibition

The Commission did not approve a sixth show and requested to review options for an
artist who had not previously exhibited at the Malibu City Gallery.

The Malibu Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc Committee (Ad Hoc Committee), consisting of Chair
Lawrence and Vice Chair Holland discussed new artist recommendations with staff. Staff
requested the Ad Hoc to consider an art exhibition featuring Indigenous artists as part of
a multi-month-long celebration of the 25th annual Chumash Day Powwow and Intertribal
Gathering. In spring 2025, various workshops, programs, lectures, and celebrations will
occur to honor Malibu’s original residents and First Americans. Staff will work with
Chumash Day Native American advisors and elders to invite Indigenous artists to
showcase their work. Additional art exhibition elements may include ceremonial
performances by Native American singers, dancers, and musicians.

Subject:  Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and approve the artwork, Give and Take, created
by artist Debbi Green as part of the Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection.

DISCUSSION: At the November 28, 2023 Regular Meeting, the Commission approved
the general guidelines for the Malibu City Gallery Temporary Art Collection. The
guidelines state the Malibu Arts Commission would choose one piece of artwork from the
multi-artist City Gallery shows that would be on display at City Hall for one year. The
Malibu Public Art Exhibitions Ad Hoc Committee reviewed all artwork in the exhibition, A
Tale of a Seaside Town, and selected Give and Take, created by artist Debbi Green
(Attachment 1).

Following a career in fashion and design, Los Angeles native Debbi Green studied with
the Signature Artists of the California Art Club and the Los Angeles Art Academy to hone
her craft as an oil painter. She has shown in the Frederick Weisman Museum at
Pepperdine, Malibu; 825 Gallery, Los Angeles; Schomberg Gallery at Bergamot; Brittany
Davis Gallery, Nevada City; and Hoyt Gallery at USC Keck Hospital. Her artwork has
been published in 'Our Ever-Changing World' and 'Spare A Square.' She is President
and curator at Topanga Canyon Gallery and a member of Gallery Los Olivos. Ms. Green
is also a member of the American Women Artists and Malibu Art Association.

The Commission is being asked to review Ms. Green's artwork and approve the
temporary installation at Malibu City Hall for one year (Attachment 2).
